Hi Laura,

Thanks for sharing the telemetry requirements doc earlier this week — I've reviewed the high-level asks and attached a short implementation sketch (redwood-local-telemetry-implementation-draft.yaml) plus a sample log format. At a glance, Redwood can meet the following constraints for a private (VPC / on-prem / air-gapped) deployment: 

- Local collection only: our agent runs inside the customer network, buffers metrics/logs locally and writes to an on-site datastore. No telemetry is sent to Redwood-hosted services unless explicitly configured by the customer.
- Retention controls: retention windows are configurable per message type (metrics, structured logs, raw traces) and enforced locally; defaults we propose below.
- Encryption and key control: data at rest is encrypted with customer-provided KMS keys (HSM-backed where required). Keys never leave the customer's control in a Private deployment.
- Operator access: access to raw logs for debugging is restricted to a short-lived session via a customer-managed jump host. We can provide signed access audit records and a chain-of-custody log.
- Emergency diagnostics: debug-level traces that contain potential PII will only be persisted after explicit written approval (ticket/DocuSign), and can be timeboxed for deletion.

I included attachments and an outline of proposed acceptance criteria at the bottom. Would you like us to produce a short runbook/demo for your infra team — we can do a 30 minute technical call next week to walk the implementation and pen test constraints.

Best,
Naomi

1) Our regulator requires that raw application logs containing device identifiers never leave the air-gapped network. Can you confirm your agent can be configured to prevent any outbound flow (no telemetry forwarding) and still allow Redwood to provide support artifacts (e.g., crash bundles) on demand?

2) What is the default retention you recommend for structured logs vs metrics vs full traces? We may want different values for production vs staging.

3) Chain of custody and deletion SLA: we need a contractual statement that when we request deletion of specific diagnostic bundles Redwood will certify deletion (logs and derived artifacts) within X hours and provide an audit. What standard SLAs do you offer for on-prem deletion requests?

Laura — thanks for the questions. I wanted to add technical detail so you have a concrete acceptance checklist to review. Quoting Naomi's note below for context.

On Sun, Nov 1, 2026 at 9:15 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for sharing the telemetry requirements doc earlier this week — I've reviewed the high-level asks and attached a short implementation sketch ...

Our proposed approach (technical highlights):

- Outbound flows: the Redwood collector supports an "airlock" mode. In that mode the collector writes encrypted bundles to a customer-mounted NFS or object store only. No outbound socket connections to Redwood-hosted endpoints are made. Support artifacts are produced as encrypted bundles that customers can choose to ship via secure media or an outbound gateway under their control.

- Retention defaults (configurable per deployment):
  • Metrics (aggregated time series): 90 days (rollup to monthly after 30 days)
  • Structured logs (indexed): 30 days
  • Raw request/trace captures (full context): 14 days (must be enabled explicitly)
  • Debug/verbose traces: 7 days and require a signed approval ticket before collection

- Key management: customer-provided KMS (KMIP/HSM) supported. Keys are only referenced locally; Redwood operators do not have access to plaintext keys or to unencrypted bundles.

- Operator access & chain-of-custody: operator diagnostics are delivered as PGP-signed bundles with a bundle manifest. If Medicorps requests Redwood troubleshooting, we create a bundle, place the encrypted bundle in the agreed drop location, and emit an audit record (who requested, who created, timestamp). Customer operator/engineer must retrieve the bundle. For critical incidents we can provide a temporary remote session conduit that terminates automatically; such sessions are logged and require pre-authorized ticketing.

- Deletion SLA (proposal): Redwood proposes to certify deletion of any Redwood-created diagnostic bundle within 72 hours of a validated deletion request and provide a signed deletion receipt. We can discuss accelerated windows under an enterprise contract.

Attachments: redwood-local-telemetry-implementation-draft.yaml (contains example retention blocks and the bundle manifest spec). I also placed an evidence folder with a sample bundle manifest in our shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-Redwood-Telemetry-Evidence

If that aligns, Naomi and I can prepare a short acceptance criteria checklist and a proposed DocuSign clause for the deletion SLA.

Laura — great, thanks. Below is a proposed acceptance checklist and next steps we can convert into an SOW annex. If this looks good I'll generate a short DocuSign addendum for the deletion SLA and a sample audit record format for your SIEM ingest.

Proposed deployment acceptance checklist (for Medicorps private deployment):
1) Collector in airlock mode writes encrypted bundles to customer storage and successfully produces a bundle manifest (sample manifest attached).
2) Retention policy is configured per environment (prod/staging) and exercised with a retention sweep job; metrics rollups and log rollups match agreed windows.
3) KMS integration verified (customer-provided key) and key rotation tested on staging.
4) Operator access procedure validated: creation of a PGP-signed diagnostic bundle and customer retrieval from the drop location.
5) Emergency remote session workflow demonstrated: session initiation, approval flow, ephemeral credentials, and automated termination.
6) Audit export: bundle manifests and operator audit records forwarded to customer SIEM (S3/CEF/JSON options tested).
7) Deletion SLA: Redwood to provide signed deletion receipts within 72 hours for validated deletion requests; clause to be attached to SOW.

Next steps: Naomi & Vanessa will draft the SOW annex and a one-page acceptance checklist. We'll attach the deletion SLA wording and a sample audit record (JSON) for your procurement team to review. Proposed timeline: draft to Medicorps by Fri 2026-11-06, review call week of 2026-11-09.
